issue.title: MissionRaw stopped working from v1.2.0 to v1.3.0
issue.body:
In my android app after uploading from io.mavsdk:mavsdk-server:1.2.1 to io.mavsdk:mavsdk-server:1.3.1 I noticed that I could not upload the mission. After downgrading to 1.2.1 the functionality was the same as before.

I could upload with 
    implementation 'io.mavsdk:mavsdk:1.2.0'
    implementation 'io.mavsdk:mavsdk-server:1.2.1'

and could not upload with 
    implementation 'io.mavsdk:mavsdk:1.3.0'
    implementation 'io.mavsdk:mavsdk-server:1.3.1'

In the log I am receiving a warning "W  Invalid sequence for ArduPilot items"  and in Wireshark I can not see any mavlink messages sent. The MISSION_COUNT message is not sent.

comments.body:

The warning is shown from here: https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/5359b58066f7b1b7a2864527aa8d91c06cfe4fd7/src/mavsdk/core/mavlink_mission_transfer.cpp#L249

I believe that the first element for Ardupilot should be the RTL waypoint, is that correct? Could it be that before, you did not have to set it, and now you do? What are you doing right now, are you setting an RTL as the first waypoint or not?

I am using Ardupilot. 

I have found that in C++. I downloaded and found that piece of code. The part that I cannot understand is that with the method of implementation of mission with MAVSDK, it makes no sense for that piece of code to make any trouble since no one has to add the mission_count message in mavlink.                     MissionRaw.MissionItem(seq++,

                        0, 0, 0.0F,
                        0)
                )

                // Set Servo ON
                missionItems.add(
                    MissionRaw.MissionItem(seq++,
                        MAV_FRAME_GLOBAL_TERRAIN_ALT, MAV_CMD_DO_SET_SERVO,

                        5.0F, sprayerIntensityPWM, 0.0F, 0.0F,
                        0, 0, 0.0F,
                        0)
                )

                // Set user preferable speed in m/s
                missionItems.add(
                    MissionRaw.MissionItem(seq++,
                        MAV_FRAME_GLOBAL_TERRAIN_ALT, MAV_CMD_DO_CHANGE_SPEED,

                    )
                )

        }

        missionItems.add(
            MissionRaw.MissionItem(seq++,
                MAV_FRAME_GLOBAL_TERRAIN_ALT, MAV_CMD_DO_SPRAYER,
                0, 1,
                0.0F, 0.0F, 0.0F, 0.0F,
                0, 0, 0.0F,
                0)
        )

        // Set Servo OFF
        missionItems.add(
            MissionRaw.MissionItem(seq++,
                MAV_FRAME_GLOBAL_TERRAIN_ALT, MAV_CMD_DO_SET_SERVO,
                0, 1,
                5.0F, 1000.0F, 0.0F, 0.0F,
                0, 0, 0.0F,
                0)
        )

        // RTL - Return To Land
        missionItems.add(
            MissionRaw.MissionItem(seq,
                MAV_FRAME_MISSION, MAV_CMD_NAV_RTL,
                0, 1,
                0.0F, 0.0F, 0.0F, 0.0F,
                0, 0, 0.0F,
                0)
        )

            0)
    )`

`        missionItems.add(

missionItems.add( MissionRaw.MissionItem(seq++, MAV_FRAME_GLOBAL_RELATIVE_ALT, MAV_CMD_NAV_WAYPOINT, 1, 1, 0.0F, 0.0F, 0.0F, Float.NaN, curPos.latitude, curPos.longitude, alt, 0) )

I think you don't want `seq++` here. The sequence should be: 0, 0, 1, 2, 3, ... Can you make sure that's what you're sending?

ok. I found the issue. My code was working on version 1.2.0 but stopped working on v1.3.0. After @julianoes last comment I started digging into Python examples and found the mission_import.py example. I added a loop to print out the elements of the example-mission.plan and noticed the correct sequence. My problem was that even when I tried with the correct sequence(0, 0, 1, 2, 3 ...) I was not using the correct sequence with current and autocontinue as shown below in example-mission.plan. The current needs to be 0 in the first mission_item(Waypoint:16) and then 1 in the second waypoint(Takeoff:22)

MissionItem: [seq: 0, frame: 5, command: 16, current: 0, autocontinue: 1, param1: 0.0, param2: 0.0, param3: 0.0, param4: 0.0, x: 473977420, y: 85455939, z: 488.7872009277344, mission_type: 0]
MissionItem: [seq: 0, frame: 3, command: 22, current: 1, autocontinue: 1, param1: 0.0, param2: 0.0, param3: 0.0, param4: nan, x: 473977420, y: 85455939, z: 50.0, mission_type: 0]
MissionItem: [seq: 1, frame: 3, command: 16, current: 0, autocontinue: 1, param1: 0.0, param2: 0.0, param3: 0.0, param4: nan, x: 473982266, y: 85455604, z: 50.0, mission_type: 0]
MissionItem: [seq: 2, frame: 3, command: 16, current: 0, autocontinue: 1, param1: 0.0, param2: 0.0, param3: 0.0, param4: nan, x: 473982493, y: 85449242, z: 50.0, mission_type: 0]
MissionItem: [seq: 3, frame: 3, command: 16, current: 0, autocontinue: 1, param1: 0.0, param2: 0.0, param3: 0.0, param4: nan, x: 473977416, y: 85449242, z: 50.0, mission_type: 0]
MissionItem: [seq: 4, frame: 2, command: 20, current: 0, autocontinue: 1, param1: 0.0, param2: 0.0, param3: 0.0, param4: 0.0, x: 0, y: 0, z: 0.0, mission_type: 0]  

When I applied the same paradigm on my code it works on both v1.2.0 and v1.3.0.

For me it is still strange that with the wrong mission instruction set I was able to work with version 1.1.0 and 1.2.0 and I could not when I upgraded to 1.3.0.

Thank you for your support. I was wrong, it was not an bug in 1.3.0 after all.

Hi @prokas-nikos,
The current sequence for mission sequence is 0,1,2,3, etc. We had incorrectly implemented ardupilot mission validation which has been now corrected and pushed to the main branch. I am not sure about the status in v1.3.0, but i believe that release was from much before the addition of ardupilot mission validation check. 

If you are using ArduPilot, I would suggest to use the main branch instead of specific tagged versions since many ardupilot related changes are in the main branch. After the release of v2.0 these should be available also in the release.

More information on how to setup and work with ArduPilot and MAVSDK are in this repository https://github.com/ykhedar/ardupilot-mavsdk which I specifically created to help devs like you get started with this combination. Give it a try and let me know if you face any problem.

> I am not sure about the status in v1.3.0, but i believe that release was from much before the addition of ardupilot mission validation check.

I backported it: https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/pull/2065

It's part of [v1.4.15](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/releases/tag/v1.4.15)

I need to update the Python wrappers to be based on top of it.
@JonasVautherin can you update the Java wrappers as well? Thanks.

Hi @ykhedar, 
thanks for the info. I will check out for sure. The reason I moved to previous versions was to locate where the issue first appeared. I am using MAVSDK one year now, and when I tried to make some changes to my app and upgrade to the latest version of MAVSDK the problem appeared.

This has been fixed in MAVSDK [v1.4.15](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/releases/tag/v1.4.15), MAVSDK-Python [v1.4.7](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK-Python/releases/tag/1.4.7), and MAVSDK-Java [1.3.2](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK-Java/releases/tag/1.3.2).

Thanks @ykhedar and @JonasVautherin.

issue.title: Mission Upload issues with Mavsdk Java and Ardupilot

repository.name: MAVSDK
repository.description: API and library for MAVLink compatible systems written in C++ 20

issue.body:
In an effort to build capabilities while testing and learning mavsdk I have been modifying some of the example code in MavSDK Java to talk with a SITL Arducopter drone.

My Environment:
	- Windows 11 host
	- Ardupilot SITL using WSL Linux ubuntu
	- Mavsdk server from [Releases](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/releases/download/v2.0.0/mavsdk_server_musl_x86_64) hosted in Alpine 3.19 docker
	-  MavSDKJava examples running from intellij gradle task

The Issue:
When attempting to start a mission upload using the code snippet below I get a "TIMEOUT" return after just a second or 2. This error happens regardless of using MissionRaw or Mission plugins.

To Reproduce:
	- run mavsdk server  v2.0 using `./mavsdk_server --sysid 10 --compid 10 udp://:14450  -p 50051`
	- Install or otherwise have ardupilot SITL on your machine
	-  add `MCTSSA=33.246358,-117.425353,200,90` to your location.txt file located at `ardupilot/Tools/autotest/`
	- run the SITL using: `sim_vehicle.py -v ArduCopter --console --map --location MCTSSA --instance 0`
	- Manually give your drone a mission of fly-to points using the draw or edit features in MavProxy or otherwise get a mission to the drone
